events.title: Execution of Anne Boleyn
events.description: Anne Boleyn, the second wife of King Henry VIII of England, was beheaded at the Tower of London after being convicted of adultery, incest, and treason on charges widely regarded as fabricated.
events.significance: Her execution cleared the way for Henry VIII to marry Jane Seymour and had lasting consequences for the English Reformation and the Tudor succession, as her daughter Elizabeth I later became one of England's greatest monarchs.

events.title: New England's Dark Day
events.description: A thick, unexplained darkness descended over parts of New England and southeastern Canada at midday, forcing people to light candles and leading many to fear the end of the world. It is now attributed to smoke from massive forest fires combined with fog and cloud cover.
events.significance: The event is one of the earliest well-documented cases of wildfire smoke causing widespread daytime darkness and became a notable moment in American religious and cultural memory.

events.title: Birth of Ho Chi Minh
events.description: Ho Chi Minh, the Vietnamese revolutionary leader, was born in Hoang Tru village, Nghe An province, in French Indochina. Traditionally his birthday is commemorated on May 19.
events.significance: He founded the Indochinese Communist Party, led the Viet Minh, and became President of North Vietnam, playing a central role in the fight against French colonial rule and in the Vietnam War.

events.title: Birth of Malcolm X
events.description: Malcolm X, born Malcolm Little in Omaha, Nebraska, became a prominent African American Muslim minister and human rights activist.
events.significance: A powerful voice for Black empowerment and self-determination during the civil rights era, he influenced the Black Power movement, and his posthumously published Autobiography remains a landmark of American literature.

events.title: Start of the Turkish War of Independence
events.description: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk landed at Samsun on the Black Sea coast to begin organizing resistance against the Allied occupation of the Ottoman Empire following World War I.
events.significance: His arrival is regarded as the beginning of the Turkish War of Independence, leading to the abolition of the Ottoman sultanate and the founding of the Republic of Turkey in 1923. The date is celebrated as a national holiday in Turkey.
